# lean-agents

This is a standalone skill. Use the current request or explicit invocation arguments as input. Read existing project instructions and only the context needed for this task. No Lean installation, CLI, configuration, or other skill is required. Do not install a workflow or create workflow files as a prerequisite. Existing project rules still apply.

Use the user's requested procedure depth; otherwise use standard depth. High adds boundary cases and stronger evidence; ultra adds cross-part consistency and contradictory evidence where relevant. Depth does not change model reasoning settings. Keep decisions in the conversation unless the project already has a suitable record or the user requests persistence.

Invocation requests delegation for the supplied task. An explicit model and xN mean up to N simultaneous workers using that model where supported; N is a ceiling, not a quota. Without a count, use only useful independent parallel tasks and obey runtime and project limits.

1. Split work into bounded tasks with acceptance checks, dependencies and exclusive file ownership. Keep planning, integration and final validation with the controller. If tasks overlap, serialize them or isolate worktrees. Show the assignment plan before dispatch.
2. Select available models and efforts from verified runtime capabilities and user preferences. Never invent model availability or silently substitute an explicitly requested model. Report unsupported settings; use inherited settings only when no explicit choice requires otherwise.
3. Pass each worker the task, relevant instructions, owned files, acceptance and minimum necessary context. Give independent reviewers a fresh context containing requirements and the shipping diff, not the author's conclusions. Do not bypass permissions or silently start metered API work.
4. Record requested and actual runtime settings when observable. Monitor blockers, resolve ownership conflicts and integrate only reviewed worker changes. Never reset or overwrite another worker's uncommitted work.
5. Validate the integrated final state with project checks and review against acceptance. Worker claims alone are not evidence. Report assignments, results, checks and remaining blockers.

If no delegation tools exist, report the limitation. Continue directly only when delegation is optional; a request requiring independent or parallel execution remains BLOCKED until that requirement can be met or changed by the user.

# lean-gate

This is a standalone skill. Use the current request or explicit invocation arguments as input. Read existing project instructions and only the context needed for this task. No Lean installation, CLI, configuration, or other skill is required. Do not install a workflow or create workflow files as a prerequisite. Existing project rules still apply.

Use the user's requested procedure depth; otherwise use standard depth. High adds boundary cases and stronger evidence; ultra adds cross-part consistency and contradictory evidence where relevant. Depth does not change model reasoning settings. Keep decisions in the conversation unless the project already has a suitable record or the user requests persistence.

1. Reuse the existing acceptance and delivery agreement; do not reopen settled scope without new evidence. Identify acceptance and the final shipping state, including new files. Find required checks in project instructions, manifests and CI. Inspect commands before execution. Missing checks are a gap, not an automatic pass; for prose-only work explain the applicable content/link validation.
2. Run relevant deterministic checks, or reuse verified results only when their inputs have not changed and project rules allow reuse. Preserve failures. Do not weaken tests, change acceptance or waive mandatory checks merely to pass.
3. Check evidence for the integrated user journey and agreed delivery destination. Identify simulated boundaries and missing end-to-end coverage; a build or unit-test pass alone does not prove an untested integration. Verify meaningful tests for behavior changes and regression evidence for bug fixes. Review must cover the final diff after validation: LOW self-check, MEDIUM focused review, HIGH fresh independent review; quality HIGH requires at least MEDIUM and VERY_HIGH requires HIGH. Report unavailable required independence as BLOCKED.
4. When called within an implementation workflow, return unmet acceptance and evidence gaps to its controller, which owns repairs and retry counts; do not start a nested repair loop. When used alone with repair authorization, fix in-scope failures, rerun affected checks and renew review. Across the task, after a second review REWORK allow one final fix-only pass and checks/review, then stop if violations remain. Missing tools or material design decisions block dependent work. Report unrelated failures and seek scope direction where fixing them would expand the task. A suspected flaky check gets at most two unchanged retries; disclose them.
5. Match each acceptance item to current evidence and synchronize existing task records. DONE requires all mandatory acceptance, validation, review and delivery conditions. BLOCKED means missing prerequisites; FAILED means demonstrated unresolved failures. List command outcomes, review coverage, skips and the next action when incomplete.

This is an agent-run completion assessment, not an automatic Stop hook, cryptographic receipt or permission guard. Never claim those enforcement guarantees. Invocation authorizes the relevant safe local checks, not deployments or unrelated external writes.

# lean-grill

This is a standalone skill. Use the current request or explicit invocation arguments as input. Read existing project instructions and only the context needed for this task. No Lean installation, CLI, configuration, or other skill is required. Do not install a workflow or create workflow files as a prerequisite. Existing project rules still apply.

Use the user's requested procedure depth; otherwise use standard depth. High adds boundary cases and stronger evidence; ultra adds cross-part consistency and contradictory evidence where relevant. Depth does not change model reasoning settings. Keep decisions in the conversation unless the project already has a suitable record or the user requests persistence.

1. Accept the existing scope and decision record; reopen settled choices only when new requirements or contradictory evidence affect them. Read the plan and its closest project evidence. Reuse settled choices rather than asking again. A clear plan can finish READY without questions.
2. Probe only relevant boundaries: goal and acceptance, actors, data ownership/lifecycle, permissions, integration contracts, failure recovery and operations. Use concrete scenarios to expose omissions or contradictions.
3. Classify each open point as NEED DECISION or SAFE ASSUMPTION. Safe assumptions are reversible, low risk and consistent with known choices. Do not assume authorization, tenant isolation, destructive behavior, retention or breaking contract semantics.
4. Resolve material choices near the beginning rather than asking one routine implementation question per phase. New material evidence may still require a targeted question later; do not restart the whole intake. Ask a small batch of questions that materially affect the result. State consequences and recommend an option when evidence supports it. Wait for answers before dependent follow-ups; independent work may continue.
5. When called within an implementation workflow, send results to its controller to continue authorized work; readiness is a stage result, not completion of implementation. Return READY, READY_WITH_ASSUMPTIONS or BLOCKED, with decisions, assumptions, open questions and affected acceptance criteria. Preserve the result in an existing project record when appropriate. This skill does not grant implementation or publication authority.

High depth walks normal flows, exceptions and recovery per relevant actor. Ultra checks cross-flow consistency in successive focused rounds. Stop when the plan is actionable; do not turn routine work into a questionnaire.

# lean-research

This is a standalone skill. Use the current request or explicit invocation arguments as input. Read existing project instructions and only the context needed for this task. 1. State the decision question, constraints and stopping condition: what evidence would be sufficient to choose or expose a concrete blocker. Read relevant local code and documentation before widening the search. Include the current approach or no change when it is a real option.
2. Build a bounded shortlist of meaningfully different approaches, usually two to five. Compare each against the same decision-relevant criteria rather than arbitrary numerical scores.
3. Use repository evidence for local behavior and primary documentation, specifications, release notes or source for external claims. Verify time-sensitive facts. Link decisive claims and record versions or dates where relevant; label facts, inferences and unknowns separately.
4. Explain trade-offs and when each leading option wins. Recommend a conditional choice, with the evidence gaps that could reverse it. Propose a targeted probe when documentation cannot settle the decision; run it only within the task's authorization.
5. Stop when the question is answered sufficiently for the task; widen the search only for a new relevant evidence gap. When called within an authorized implementation workflow, return the decision evidence to its controller to continue that work. Return a concise comparison, recommendation and unresolved questions. Research does not itself authorize implementation, dependencies, paid services or external writes.

High depth broadens relevant candidates and corroborates decisive claims. Ultra investigates the strongest options in depth and seeks contradictory evidence. Repeated vendor pages are not independent corroboration; disclose sparse evidence instead of manufacturing certainty.

description: Own an end-to-end implementation request from initial decisions to verified delivery, coordinating available Lean skills without repeated planning or manual handoffs.

# lean-run

Use this as the controller for a request to carry work through completion. A proposal-only request still ends at the proposal. Follow project instructions and the user's authorized scope. This skill works alone: companion skills are optional, and no Lean runtime, workflow directory or installation step is required.

## Establish the delivery agreement

Read the relevant project instructions, existing decisions and closest source before asking questions. Reuse verified repository context and commands while their inputs remain unchanged. Discover only what this task needs.

State the outcome, included behavior, observable acceptance, constraints, verification method and delivery destination. Keep this to a sentence for a mechanical change. For substantial work, keep a compact record of decisions, remaining work, evidence, blockers and next action in the conversation or an existing project record. Create persistent workflow files only when requested. Use the requested procedure depth; otherwise use standard. Depth changes investigation detail, not acceptance or model settings.

Resolve consequential business rules, permissions, data lifecycle and external-contract choices near the beginning. Batch the necessary questions, explain consequences and recommend an option when evidence supports it. Decide reversible implementation details yourself using project conventions. A clear implementation request already authorizes matching work: do not add an approval round for the plan. Wait for missing material answers before dependent work; elapsed time is not an answer. Continue independent work.

Default to verified changes in the current workspace when no delivery destination is specified. A requested PR, deployment or other destination is part of acceptance and needs matching authorization and tools. Do all authorized preparatory work before any required final approval. Do not infer permission to publish, spend money or change provider settings from the word "end-to-end".

## Route only when useful

Discover which companion skills are actually available and read a selected skill before applying it. Do not load or invoke every skill as a checklist. Pass the settled agreement, relevant decisions, current content, evidence and remaining question; use the result to continue the original request. A stage result is not a reason to ask the user to invoke the next skill.

| Need | Optional companion |
| --- | --- |
| Select a different requested repository | `lean-target` |
| Discover unknown project commands and conventions | `lean-init` |
| Bound acceptance or resolve material ambiguity | `lean-scope`, `lean-grill` |
| Answer a technical question that affects implementation | `lean-research` |
| Implement and verify the agreed behavior | `lean-task` |
| Delegate useful independent work when authorized and supported | `lean-agents` |
| Review current changes and assess completion evidence | `lean-review`, `lean-gate` |
| Apply a requested procedure depth | `lean-effort` |
| Update skills or evaluate model configuration when explicitly requested | `lean-update`, `lean-model-update` |

If a companion is absent, perform the corresponding procedure below directly. Missing a skill is not a blocker; missing a required capability can be. This invocation does not itself request parallel agents. Keep one owner of scope, integration, repair counts and final delivery, even when workers are used.

## Implement and prove the outcome

1. Classify risk as LOW, MEDIUM or HIGH and quality as STANDARD, HIGH or VERY_HIGH, reusing established classifications. Consequential security, destructive data and breaking external-contract changes are HIGH risk. Implement only the work needed for acceptance; do not add adjacent cleanup or features.
2. Add meaningful tests for changed behavior. For a bug, reproduce the regression and verify it passes after repair; disclose when reproduction is unavailable. Run affected checks during iteration and required project checks on the final content. Inspect unfamiliar commands before execution and preserve unrelated work.
3. Exercise the relevant user journey through the integrated components, from its input to an observable result, with important failure cases. For non-UI work use an appropriate interface, such as an API, CLI or artifact consumer. Identify the environment, commands/actions, expected and observed outcomes, and simulated boundaries. Unit tests, builds and mocks alone do not establish an untested live integration. When live access is unavailable, finish useful authorized work and report the unmet acceptance; do not silently replace required end-to-end evidence with a simulation.
4. Review the final diff, including new files, after deterministic validation. LOW permits an acceptance self-check; MEDIUM requires focused correctness/regression review; HIGH requires a fresh independent reviewer. Quality HIGH requires at least MEDIUM review and VERY_HIGH requires HIGH. Required independence without authorized, available tools is BLOCKED, not a self-issued independent PASS.
5. Repair in-scope failures, rerun affected checks and renew review of changed content. Reuse evidence only when its inputs, relevant environment and acceptance are unchanged and project rules allow it. Maintain the requested destination as part of delivery; local success alone does not satisfy an authorized PR or deployment request.

## Keep progress finite

- Advance as soon as the current stage has sufficient evidence. Never stop at a plan, research result, worker report or review PASS when implementation or delivery remains authorized and unfinished.
- Reopen a settled decision only for a new requirement or contradictory evidence. Update the affected acceptance and work; do not restart unrelated discovery. New material decisions may still require a targeted user answer mid-task.
- Research must have a decision question and a stopping condition. Stop when evidence supports the decision, or return the concrete missing fact; do not widen the investigation without a task-relevant reason.
- Each repair attempt must state the new evidence or hypothesis and the check that will distinguish it. Stop repeating an approach that yields no new information. A suspected flaky check permits at most two unchanged retries, disclosed in the result.
- Count review REWORK results across the whole task, including companion calls and resumed work. After the second REWORK, allow one final fix-only pass and its verification/review; if mandatory findings remain, stop with FAILED and the unresolved findings. A missing prerequisite is BLOCKED. Never reset counters by re-invoking a skill or starting a nested workflow.
- Do not weaken acceptance, disable checks or omit mandatory work to claim success. Separate unrelated failures and seek scope direction only when their repair would expand the request. Continue any independent authorized work before reporting a blocker.

## Close with evidence

Match every acceptance item, including delivery, to evidence for the current state. Record commands/actions, working directory or environment, outcomes, review coverage and any limits. Keep progress updates short and tied to changed facts; do not ask "shall I continue?" for already authorized work.

Return DONE only when all mandatory acceptance, validation, review and delivery conditions hold. Return BLOCKED for missing prerequisites and FAILED for demonstrated unresolved failures, identifying affected acceptance, completed work and the exact next action. READY and PASS from a companion describe that stage only. Never call the whole request complete with mandatory work still outstanding. These are agent-run procedures, not enforced hooks or a guarantee of success on every task.

1. Read the request, closest source files and existing decisions. Reuse settled choices. Skip a formal specification for trivial mechanical work unless requested.
2. Reuse an existing delivery agreement rather than generating a second specification. Include the verification method and delivery destination (workspace by default, or the requested PR/deployment). State the goal, included behavior, exclusions, acceptance criteria, constraints, assumptions and likely affected components. For multi-part work, list bounded tasks and dependencies; do not silently expand into adjacent improvements.
3. Distinguish reversible implementation choices from unresolved material decisions about security, ownership, business rules, data lifecycle or external contracts. Ask only for decisions that change the result, explaining the options and their consequences.
4. A clear implementation request already approves matching scope: present it and continue. A specification-only request stops at the specification. Wait for missing material decisions or approval explicitly required by project instructions; elapsed time is not approval.
5. When called within an implementation workflow, return the agreed scope and unresolved decisions to its controller; a scope result does not complete that implementation request. Keep scope current as requirements arrive. Record replacements instead of quietly dropping acceptance items. Material expansions need a user decision before dependent work. At completion, map each acceptance item to evidence and disclose deferred work.

At high depth, cover actors, normal flows, boundaries and recovery. At ultra depth, check states, cross-feature interactions and rollout/rollback constraints where relevant. Stop when acceptance is observable and remaining uncertainty is explicit.

# lean-task

This is a standalone skill. Use the current request or explicit invocation arguments as input. Read existing project instructions and only the context needed for this task. No Lean installation, CLI, configuration, or other skill is required. Do not install a workflow or create workflow files as a prerequisite. Existing project rules still apply.

Use the user's requested procedure depth; otherwise use standard depth. High adds boundary cases and stronger evidence; ultra adds cross-part consistency and contradictory evidence where relevant. Depth does not change model reasoning settings. Keep decisions in the conversation unless the project already has a suitable record or the user requests persistence.

1. Reuse supplied acceptance, decisions and classifications instead of repeating intake. State risk (LOW, MEDIUM or HIGH), quality (STANDARD, HIGH or VERY_HIGH), and observable acceptance before edits. Use HIGH risk for consequential security, destructive data or breaking external-contract changes. Respect the project's own contract format if present.
2. Use the agreed scope; draft only missing scope needed to satisfy the request. A clear implementation request authorizes matching work. Clarify material ambiguity before dependent work; continue independent work. Use existing project records when required, otherwise keep the plan in chat.
3. Implement within scope. When called within a larger workflow, its controller owns delivery and repair counts; return results to it without asking the user to invoke another stage. Report progress at meaningful phase transitions: scope, implement, test, validate, review, complete. Delegate only when authorized and available, with exclusive file ownership and a bounded assignment; otherwise work directly unless delegation is mandatory.
4. Add meaningful tests for behavior changes. For a bug, demonstrate the regression before the fix and passing afterward. Run affected checks during iteration, then required project checks on the final content. Do not weaken checks to make them pass.
5. Exercise the relevant integrated user journey to its observable outcome and important failure cases using the project's UI, API, CLI or artifact interface. Record the environment, actions and results; identify mocks and untested boundaries. Required end-to-end coverage cannot be replaced silently by unit tests or a build. Review the final diff including new files after deterministic validation. LOW uses an acceptance self-check; MEDIUM uses a focused correctness/regression review; HIGH requires a fresh independent reviewer. Quality HIGH has at least MEDIUM review; VERY_HIGH has HIGH review. If required independence is unavailable, report BLOCKED rather than claim completion. Review fixes require renewed affected validation and review.
6. Keep one repair history across calls: after a second review REWORK, allow one final fix-only pass and renewed checks/review, then report remaining violations as FAILED. Missing prerequisites are BLOCKED. Check every acceptance item against current evidence, disclose skips and limitations, and synchronize existing records. DONE requires acceptance, validation, required review and the agreed delivery destination; missing prerequisites mean BLOCKED, demonstrated unresolved failures mean FAILED. Report outcome, changes, tests, review and remaining work. A commit, push or publication requires matching user authorization.

This updates skills, not a project runtime. Source: https://github.com/aussadawut-dev/lean-skills. It works when only this skill is installed.

1. Inspect which standalone skills are actually installed, their source/version metadata and installation scope. Resolve symlinks to canonical locations. Do not assume every core skill is installed or confuse project-local workflow skills with this standalone collection.
2. Read the installed skills CLI help and current upstream documentation before choosing commands. Fetch candidate content into a temporary directory without replacing the installed copy. Pin the candidate revision and compare only the requested installed skills; note local customizations and missing source/version evidence.
3. Show the concrete update plan, conflicts, source revision and preserved files. Keep modified skills unchanged until the user chooses how to handle the conflict. A preview-only request stops here; an explicit update request authorizes a matching conflict-free update, not installing extra skills or changing project configuration.
4. Back up each affected canonical directory and its installation metadata before replacement, recording a usable restore path. Use the existing installer when it supports the intended scope and pinned revision. Do not use a bulk update that also changes unrelated skills. If pinning or backup cannot be verified, stop before mutation and explain the missing capability.
5. Validate installed frontmatter, file completeness, references and discovery links. Restore from the backup on a failed update only while affected files have not changed since this operation; otherwise preserve state and report the conflict. Report updated skills, revision, checks, preserved changes and rollback location.

Never install the full workflow as part of a skill update. Do not commit, push or alter model/provider permissions as an incidental update step.
